faqHeaderData.heading:
Common Questions on 
 Ballroom AV Solutions

faqData.question: How long does a ballroom AV setup take?
faqData.answer: Physical installation on site typically requires two to four weeks following design approval and equipment delivery. Projects involving custom ceiling rigging or large LED display walls fall toward the longer end of that timeline. GS IT structures the overall ballroom AV setup schedule to align with venue availability and pre-site preparation.

faqData.question: Can the installation go ahead while our hotel keeps hosting events?
faqData.answer: Yes, system integration can proceed without disrupting your venue's ongoing booking schedule. Drilling, ceiling work, and primary cable pulls can be scheduled during after-hours or non-event windows. Divisible halls allow our team to work on one partitioned segment while remaining areas host guest functions normally.

faqData.question: What do you need from us to prepare a ballroom AV proposal?
faqData.answer: An architectural floor plan with ceiling heights, reflected ceiling plans (RCP), and existing electrical layouts provides the baseline for initial design. Target seating capacities across your regular room configurations help us calculate screen sizes and audio coverage. These details allow GS IT to build precise ballroom AV design solutions with minimal revision cycles.

faqData.question: Do we need acoustic treatment in our ballroom?
faqData.answer: Acoustic treatment becomes necessary when reflective surfaces like marble or glass degrade speech intelligibility. GS IT conducts site measurements when designing a ballroom AV solution to identify flutter echoes. Where DSP tuning alone cannot resolve sound reflection issues, we recommend targeted acoustic drapes or wall panels.

faqData.question: How many wireless microphones does our ballroom need?
faqData.answer: Microphone quantities depend directly on the peak presentation demands of your venue. Simple banquets need two handheld channels for speeches, whereas corporate galas require additional mics and wireless options for panel speakers. We configure ballroom audio visual solutions around your busiest event formats with extra receiver slots available.

faqData.question: Can our ballroom ceiling carry LED screens and line arrays?
faqData.answer: Overhead structural capacity depends on dedicated rigging points and ceiling framework ratings. GS IT confirms load ratings with the venue and its structural engineer before specifying heavy display arrays for a ballroom AV solution in Dubai. If overhead rigging points prove insufficient, ground-supported or wall-mounted options provide reliable alternatives.

faqData.question: Should our ballroom use an LED wall or projection?
faqData.answer: LED walls stay bright under full house lighting and suit launches and galas. Projection costs less for very large images and the screens can retract when not in use. Many venues pair an LED wall at the main stage with projection in the divided sections.

faqData.question: Do wireless microphones need approval in the UAE?
faqData.answer: Yes, all wireless audio equipment in the UAE must use TDRA-approved frequency bands and type-approved hardware. GS IT supplies compliant wireless systems and performs RF spectrum scans on site to identify clear transmission channels. This step prevents signal overlap with nearby radio infrastructure in dense hospitality zones.

faqData.question: Will we need an AV technician on site for each event?
faqData.answer: Routine events run without dedicated technical staff because automated touch screen controls manage basic audio and display presets. In most of our ballroom AV setups, one preset loads the microphones and screens along with the lighting scene. Large galas with live bands or complex show cues still benefit from a dedicated operator at the mixing console.

faqData.question: Can visiting DJs and bands connect to our ballroom sound system?
faqData.answer: Yes. We install stage boxes and audio tie-in panels near the stage for this purpose. Visiting crews can plug their mixer into the ballroom's sound system, and the DSP protects the speakers from sudden signal overload. Modern ballroom technology ensures that in-house microphone configurations and core room presets stay completely untouched for regular venue operations.

faqData.question: Can our ballroom host hybrid events?
faqData.answer: Yes. PTZ cameras and a streaming encoder can send the stage feed to your preferred online meeting platform. Remote speakers can appear on the main screens and be heard through the room system. A dedicated network segment helps keep the stream stable during the event.

faqData.question: Do you provide monitoring and support after handover?
faqData.answer: Post-handover monitoring and proactive technical maintenance are available through an annual maintenance contract (AMC) with GS IT. AMC subscribers receive routine system checks and scheduled site visits under defined response windows. Outside an active AMC, project scope ends at handover sign-off, and future service calls are quoted individually.
